study: Wiggins et al. 2019, RISE (Research leads Improving Students' Education) whole-school research-use program, EEF eval (UCL IoE)
eval_evidence: EEF efficacy trial 'independently evaluated by a team from UCL Institute of Education' (Meg Wiggins et al.); the program was developed and delivered by a separate party (Huntington School, York).
developer_evidence: The RISE programme was 'developed and delivered by a team from Huntington School in York', which trained the school Research Leads and ran workshops for headteachers and subject leads.
cascade_evidence: Lead-teacher cascade: the Huntington team trained/supported a senior teacher 'Research Lead' in each school, who was then responsible for promoting and supporting research use throughout the school's teachers (>=1 extra hop to classroom teachers).
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools 'continued with business as usual'; no RISE programme, Research Lead role, or research-use training.
coaching_evidence: Support consisted of training/workshops for Research Leads, headteachers, and subject leads (attendance high over 30 months); no ongoing in-class coaching of classroom teachers.
student_dose_evidence: RISE is a whole-school, research-informed improvement program acting through teacher/leader practice; no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Program newly introduced to all schools at once; outcomes span an end-of-Year-1 GCSE cohort (Cohort A, exposed 1 year) and an end-of-Year-2 cohort (Cohort B, exposed 2 years). First measurement wave is the first implementation year, so coded first_year (note: a 2-year-dose cohort also exists).
